notes: Evidence and scope qualifications
This is a verified public capability matrix, not a complete proprietary opcode/throughput specification. Apple gated CPU guide and unpublished GPU/ANE ISA prevent a literal exhaustive comparison.

LLVM 23.1 Host.cpp maps M4/DONAN and M4 Pro/Max/BRAVA to apple-m4; M5/HIDRA and M5 Pro/Max/SOTRA to apple-m5. Family grouping is therefore explicitly supported by LLVM. It remains a compiler model rather than independent per-SKU hardware validation.
M5 Pro/Max have 6 super plus 12 new performance cores at maximum; base M5 has 4 super plus 6 efficiency. Do not transfer E-core benchmarks or full per-core performance models from base M5 to Pro/Max.

LLVM apple-m4/apple-m5 start with Armv8.7 plus selected extensions. Do not infer all features from Armv9.2 marketing labels. LLVM tests explicitly warn FEAT_MPAM and FEAT_SEL2 are inherited in model despite absence on hardware.
Compiler model, silicon, OS visibility, process permissions, framework implementation and workload dispatch are separate gates.

First named target known: upstream Clang 19 apple-m4, Clang 22 apple-m5. Individual instructions may be emitted with earlier extension-aware compilers; Apple Clang version numbers are not upstream LLVM version numbers.

Native CPU SME exists on M4; the M5 news is SME 2.1 and non-widening FP16/BF16 accumulate plus CSSC/HBC/security changes. Neither SME nor BF16 input->FP32 accumulation nor LUTI2/4 generally is new to M5.

No Apple-hardware tests were run for this merge. Public first-hand measurements and uploaded host reports are attributed separately. The uploaded probe paths refer to unattached Mac files, so the native outcomes have not been independently reproduced.
A non-existent sysctl name is unknown, not a hardware absence. Read exact keys and value/error; VMs may mask CPU extensions even if host supports them.

I8MM: the uploaded M4 Pro/26.6 and base-M5/26.2 Darwin readings both report 1. Older sampled M4 system-register/VM output disagrees with LLVM and native reports; this does not establish absence on M4. Use native hw.optional.arm.FEAT_I8MM for the actual device/process environment.

The uploaded CPU observations are on M4 Pro macOS 26.6 seed and base M5 macOS 26.2. They do not establish first enabling OS minors or availability on the other four chips. Use runtime checks, supported native macOS, process permissions and an extension-aware compiler.

LLVM 22.1.0 through checked 22.1.8 Host.cpp still defaults unknown M5 hosts to apple-m4; LLVM 23.1.0 adds M5 and Pro/Max detection. Explicit -mcpu=apple-m5 works in LLVM 22; -mcpu=native is a separate version gate.

notes: Verification on the actual Mac — research did not execute these hardware tests

1. Record exact Mac/chip configuration, macOS build, Xcode/tool packages, model hash, target spec, shapes/dtypes, compression recipe and compute-unit configuration. Repeat the same workload for each comparison.
https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coreml/analyzing-a-core-ml-model-s-performance-in-xcode.md

2. Compile the CoreML package, then load MLComputePlan with the same MLModelConfiguration. Traverse operations and save supported/preferred devices and relative estimated cost. Do not report these estimates as measured per-operation durations.
https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coreml/mlcomputeplan-1w21n.md
https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coreml/analyzing-a-core-ml-model-s-performance-in-xcode.md

3. Run Xcode Performance reports on the actual target device for All, CPU-only, CPU+GPU and CPU+ANE where appropriate. Compare compilation, uncached/cached load, first prediction, median and variability; inspect placement/incompatibility hints and export the reports.
https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coreml/analyzing-a-core-ml-model-s-performance-in-xcode.md

4. Profile the integrated app in Instruments to relate model activity to actual runtime CPU/GPU/ANE work, synchronization, specialization and memory behavior. For CoreAI use its debug gauge, Instruments template and CoreAI Debugger. Xcode model timing reports alone do not measure memory or power.
https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coreml/analyzing-a-core-ml-model-s-performance-in-xcode.md
https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coreai/inspecting-debugging-and-profiling-core-ai-models.md
https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2023/10049/

5. Validate outputs against the source model and a FP32 reference on representative inputs and supported shape/state sequences before evaluating reduced precision. Check NaN/Inf and task-appropriate tolerances/quality. If needed, use experimental MLModelComparator/Validator to find divergent intermediate operations; CoreAI Debugger can compare reference tensor outputs.
https://apple.github.io/coremltools/docs-guides/source/mlmodel-debugging-perf-utilities.html
https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coreai/inspecting-debugging-and-profiling-core-ai-models.md

6. Report format support, selected device, observed kernel path, numerical quality and measured performance separately. A dtype enum, compressed file, compute-unit allowance or lower latency does not alone prove native precision instructions. No hardware execution was performed in this research.
https://apple.github.io/coremltools/docs-guides/source/opt-quantization-perf.html
https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/196916
